title: Strict pullback of simplicial sets preserves all small colimits in a slice
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and simplicial maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and small categorical colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], in a fixed universe. For a simplicial set $B$, the slice $\mathrm{sSet}_{/B}$ has objects maps $X\to B$ and morphisms commuting triangles. It has all small colimits: the underlying simplicial set of a colimit is formed degreewise in sets, with its induced map to $B$. For any simplicial map $p:E\to B$, define $p^*(q:X\to B)=(E\times_B X\to E)$, with the induced maps on morphisms; the strict pullback has $n$-simplices the pairs $(e,x)$ with $p_n(e)=q_n(x)$. For every small category $I$, including the empty category, and diagram $X:I\to\mathrm{sSet}_{/B}$, the canonical comparison in $\mathrm{sSet}_{/E}$ is an isomorphism, natural in $X$:
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}(E\times_B X_i)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ E\times_B\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}X_i.$$
Equivalently, $p^*$ preserves all small colimits. No fibrancy, monomorphism, or connectedness condition is imposed on $p$ or $I$.

source.place: Proposition 3.7, printed p. 6, specialized degreewise to simplicial sets; read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag for this exact simplicial statement; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Forget the maps to $B$ for the moment. A simplicial set is a presheaf on $\Delta$ by [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For every $n$, apply [lem-coef-small-set-colimit-quotient] to the small set diagram $i\mapsto(X_i)_n$, obtaining $L_n$ with elements $[i,x]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-colimits-sectionwise] with $\mathcal C=\Delta$ and $\mathcal A=\mathbf{Set}$: these sets assemble into a simplicial set $L$, with operators $L(\alpha)[i,x]=[i,X_i(\alpha)x]$, and its cocone $X_i\to L$ is colimiting in simplicial sets. This applies to empty $I$ as well. All indexing sets and degreewise quotients lie in the fixed universe.

Write $q_i:X_i\to B$ for the structure maps. Since the diagram arrows are over $B$, the $q_i$ form a cocone, so the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $q:L\to B$ with $q[i,x]=q_i(x)$. For any cocone $X_i\to Y$ over $B$, the unique underlying simplicial map $u:L\to Y$ is over $B$: both $q_Yu$ and $q$ have composites $q_i$ on all cocone legs, hence are equal by colimit uniqueness. The same uniqueness proves the slice universal property. Thus $L\to B$ is the slice colimit. This reasoning also applies to a diagram over $E$.

The sets $P_{i,n}=\{(e,x)\in E_n\times(X_i)_n:p_n(e)=q_{i,n}(x)\}$ have operators $(e,x)\mapsto(E(\alpha)e,X_i(\alpha)x)$, well-defined by naturality of $p$ and $q_i$. Functor laws hold componentwise. A simplicial map to $P_i$ is uniquely a pair of maps to $E$ and $X_i$ having equal composites to $B$, since this is true on every simplex. Hence $P_i$ is the strict pullback. An arrow $a:i\to j$ induces $(e,x)\mapsto(e,X(a)x)$; these formulas define the diagram $p^*X$ and the functor $p^*$ on slice morphisms. The same construction gives $P=E\times_B L$.

source.place: Definitions 016A and 0175; componentwise verification of the displayed pair construction

proof.text: Use the colimit presentations of steps 1-2 also for $p^*X$, and put $C=\operatorname{colim}_i P_i$ over $E$. The maps $P_i\to P$, $(e,x)\mapsto(e,[i,x])$, commute with simplicial operators and diagram arrows. They therefore induce the canonical slice comparison $\theta:C\to P$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In degree $n$ it sends $[i,(e,x)]$ to $(e,[i,x])$. It is surjective: given $(e,l)\in P_n$, the representative clause of [lem-coef-small-set-colimit-quotient] writes $l=[i,x]$. Then $p_n(e)=q_n(l)=q_{i,n}(x)$, so $(e,x)\in P_{i,n}$ is a preimage. If $I$ is empty, $L_n=C_n=\varnothing$ and therefore $P_n=\varnothing$; the same comparison is the unique map between empty sets.

source.place: Tag 002U, section-limit-sets; quotient representatives and the elementary comparison formula

proof.text: For injectivity, suppose $\theta_n[i,(e,x)]=\theta_n[j,(e',y)]$. Then $e=e'$ and $[i,x]=[j,y]$. By [lem-coef-small-set-colimit-quotient], $(i,x)$ and $(j,y)$ are related by the equivalence relation generated by arrow relations. Along an arrow relation $z'=X(a)z$, one has $q_{\mathrm{target}(a),n}(z')=q_{\mathrm{source}(a),n}(z)$ because $X(a)$ is over $B$. Thus every element in a finite chain of arrow relations or reversed arrow relations connecting $x$ to $y$ has base value $p_n(e)$. Pair each element of the chain with this same $e$. Each forward relation becomes the arrow relation $(e,z)\mapsto(e,X(a)z)$ for the diagram $P_i$, and a reversed relation becomes its reverse. Reflexivity gives a chain of length zero; symmetry reverses a chain and transitivity concatenates chains. Consequently the lifted chain identifies $[i,(e,x)]$ with $[j,(e,y)]$ in $C_n$, by the quotient equality clause of the same cited node. This proves injectivity without replacing a general diagram by a filtered one.

source.place: Tag 002U, section-limit-sets; elementary lifting of the generating equivalence relation in a fixed fiber

proof.text: Each $\theta_n$ is bijective by steps 4-5. Its inverses form a simplicial map: for an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the already proved identity $P(\alpha)\theta_n=\theta_m C(\alpha)$ implies $C(\alpha)\theta_n^{-1}=\theta_m^{-1}P(\alpha)$ by composing with the inverses. The inverse is over $E$ since $\theta$ preserves the first coordinate and is bijective. Thus $\theta$ is an isomorphism in the slice. For a morphism of diagrams $f:X\to X'$ over $B$, both composites in the comparison naturality square send a representative $[i,(e,x)]$ to $(e,[i,f_i(x)])$. Every simplex has a representative by [lem-coef-small-set-colimit-quotient], so the composites are equal. Hence the isomorphism is natural in $X$. This is precisely preservation of all small colimits as defined by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
